sources.title: District Gujranwala, Geography
sources.scope: Present-day regional context only. Administrative boundaries and distances are not imported into the historical map.

claims.observation: The study describes red brick, plaster and wood in the surviving facade.
claims.limit: Surviving fabric does not establish the precise 1792 finish, brick size or repair state.

claims.observation: The architectural study and modern photograph show courts, arches and attached columns.
claims.limit: The playable home is not that building's measured plan. Its movement routes remain the existing authored ones.

claims.observation: The district description places Gujranwala in relation to the Chenab and neighbouring districts.
claims.limit: This reference supplies regional context, not the positions of 1792 streets, waterways or buildings.

elements.title: Brick and plaster compound walls
elements.choice: Analytic masonry material on existing collision geometry. Brick dimensions, colors and wear are art-direction parameters.

elements.title: Courtyard panels and shallow arches
elements.choice: Ten attached blind bays, timber screens and cornices. These are solid-backed panels, not walk-through doors. Existing entrance routes are unchanged.

elements.title: Stable beams and market vessels
elements.choice: Original timber-beam and pottery meshes on existing roofs/counter. No new craft recipe or supply quantity is inferred.

elements.title: Low settlement silhouette
elements.choice: Sixteen authored houses outside the existing test boundary. Visual backdrop, not additional traversable streets or historic property locations.

excluded: precise historical monument replicas without a dated reconstruction
tourism-restoration mosaics or fountains treated as original fabric
rumoured tunnels treated as verified routes
expanded playable bounds without a separate collision/save migration
